beliefs.practice: Store the cluster connection string in an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit it; for production use a secret store such as Azure Key Vault and grant your app managed identity access to fetch it at runtime.

Reuse a single MongoClient instance per process (create at startup, share across threads/tasks) and close it on shutdown; avoid making a new client per request. Tune pool sizes with maxPoolSize/minPoolSize in the connection options.

Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and rate limiting: catch 429 (Request Rate Too Large) and network/timeout errors, use the server-provided Retry-After header when present, and retry with jitter.

Provision throughput (RU/s) appropriate for indexing and vector search: estimate ingestion, embedding compute and query load and use autoscale or set sufficient RU/s for the sample database/collection to avoid frequent 429s; increase RU during index creation and bulk loads.

Create conventional indexes on fields used for filtering/aggregation (e.g., channel, topic tags, created_at) and consider a compound index for common compound predicates (e.g., {channel:1, created_at:1}) to accelerate the aggregation pipelines.
For time-based retention, use a TTL policy/index (expireAfterSeconds) to automatically purge raw feedback after the retention period rather than manual delete jobs.

Store deterministic embeddings with a fixed vector dimension and a field name (e.g., embedding: [float,...]) and validate length on write; if using cosine similarity, also store normalized vectors (unit length) to simplify search/score calculations.

When creating vector indexes tune ANN index parameters for HNSW/IVF: set a sensible M (e.g., 16–64) and efConstruction (e.g., 100–200) at index creation to balance recall and memory; set efSearch at query time (higher for better recall).

If the managed cluster returns CommandNotSupported for vector/text index creation, fall back to storing embeddings and performing nearest-neighbor matching client-side (or with manual approximate search logic) and keep index-creation attempts guarded with graceful fallback.

Design documents to avoid frequent large rewrites: use atomic update operators ($set, $push, $inc) to modify only changed fields (e.g., add sentinel fields sentiment, topics, embedding) instead of replacing entire documents on enrichment.
Use bulk operations (insert_many, bulk_write) when ingesting batches of feedback to reduce round-trips and improve throughput, and throttle bulk size to avoid exhausting RU/s during large loads.

Enforce a lightweight schema/validation (JSON Schema validator) at the collection level to require essential fields (text, channel, created_at, embedding length, sentiment) so downstream aggregation and embedding logic can assume schema invariants.

Keep the embedding dimension and vector data type consistent across documents (e.g., 1536 floats) and store metadata about the embedder (model name + version) alongside each embedding to allow model upgrades without corrupting search semantics.

Monitor slow queries and index usage; use explain() on expensive aggregation pipelines and create/adjust indexes based on the query plan. Regularly inspect cluster metrics (RU consumption, index storage, latency).

Handle consistency choices explicitly: rely on the cluster/account consistency configuration for cross-region reads; avoid assuming per-operation strong consistency unless the API explicitly supports overriding consistency per operation.

Avoid storing raw PII in cleartext; for identifiers or sensitive customer fields either omit them from the enrichment store, pseudonymize or encrypt them with client-side field-level encryption before storing.
Use deterministic document IDs or a composite unique key (e.g., source_channel + source_id) to make ingests idempotent and simplify deduplication of the same feedback item across channels.

For aggregation pipelines that compute time-series sentiment (by channel/topic/time window), ensure created_at is indexed and store timestamps in UTC and as an ISODate so $bucket or $dateTrunc operations are efficient.

When embedding or enriching via LLMs, perform the extraction (sentiment, topics, quote) deterministically where possible, validate the output, and store source_text and the canonical extracted fields to allow reprocessing if parsing prompts/models change.

Regularly back up important data and know the provider’s backup/restore options; for critical datasets enable continuous or frequent backups and test restore procedures rather than relying solely on exported JSON snapshots.
